patch.value: Combining an annotation or linked-artifact mutation with a universal output control is refused untyped: code command_failed and pm --help examples instead of a stable code and a retry without the control

Found 2026-11-08 while verifying PR 1685 review findings. validateReadOutputOptions (src/sdk/read-output-contracts.ts) refuses a comments, notes, learnings, files, docs or package-catalog mutation combined with a universal output control (--output-budget, --output-cursor, --output-limit, --output-include, --output-session) with the message "Universal output controls cannot be combined with a <command> mutation." The refusal carries no typed code. pm learnings <id> --add x --output-cursor bad --json reports code command_failed, required "Adjust command input or tracker state and retry." and examples "pm --help" and "pm <command> --help". So an agent cannot key its recovery on the refusal, and the guidance never says what to do: run the mutation without the output control, or read with the output control after the write. Measured on the PR 1685 head with the built CLI in a sandbox tracker. Expected: a stable code (for example read_output_mutation_conflict), the offending output flags, and a suggested retry without them, through CLI, SDK and MCP. The refusal-closure census should count the new code. Duplicate check: searched universal output controls mutation refusal code. pm-479ggz (closed) rejected the controls for package manage diagnostics, and pm-f05lsg (open) measures recovery closure in general. Neither types this refusal.

The mutation and output-control refusal carries a stable typed code that the error catalog and refusal-closure census include; The refusal names the offending output flags and suggests a retry of the mutation without them through CLI, SDK and MCP
In a sandbox tracker run pm learnings <id> --add x --output-cursor bad --json and read the code, required and examples fields

value.text: Implementation evidence, branch fix/annotation-read-fidelity. validateReadOutputOptions now throws readOutputMutationConflict. Fields: code read_output_mutation_conflict (exit 2, catalogued in generated-error-code-catalog-part-2.ts and listed in docs/generated/REFUSAL_CLOSURE_CENSUS.md); field (the first control); details.surface; details.output_controls (CLI flags); details.output_option_keys (the camelCase or snake_case keys the SDK or MCP caller supplied); details.mutation_options; a required line that says to retry without the controls and read with them separately; and runnable per-surface examples. HYBRID_READ_MUTATION_KEYS is now typed over exactly the six hybrid surfaces, so every surface has examples and no unreachable fallback exists. CLI: src/cli/runtime/read-output-mutation-retry.ts rewrites the recovery as the caller's argv without each control token and the value it consumed. It is wired into repairInvocationRecovery in main.ts beside the other mutation retries and binds an environment-selected tracker the same way. Flag arity comes from scanOptionTokens in projection-retry.ts, which now reports each token's consumed value, so arity has one source. The error path records argv as 'item comments ...', so the repair resolves the two-token command path before scanning. Verified with the built CLI: 'pm learnings <id> --add x --output-limit 3 --output-cursor=abc --output-row-contract --json' exits 2 with suggested_retry 'pm item learnings <id> --add x --json', and that retry runs. MCP tools/call returns the code, details and output_option_keys.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Review fix on PR 1688 (Codex P1 and Greptile P2). The retry scanner reads value arity from vocabulary rows, which leave command flags such as --message untyped. Global normalization also lets a value-taking control swallow the next option: in 'comments pm-one --add kept --message --output-limit --pm-path /tmp/A --output-budget 500', --output-limit takes --pm-path as its value and the tracker path becomes the --message text. The rebuilt retry 'comments pm-one --add kept --message /tmp/A' was faithful to that parse, but it replayed the misparse as a clean write to the environment tracker. repairReadOutputMutationRecovery now withholds the retry in two cases. First, when a control consumed a flag-like token. Second, when a control directly follows a value-taking option, using the arity from enrichCliFlagInvocationContracts, which the flag-invocation parity gate verifies against the parser. In both cases the refusal still names the controls to drop. Specs cover the Codex argv, the dash-led budget case, the Greptile argv, '--add --output-limit', inline and boolean predecessors, a control before the command and a trailing control. A two-tracker CLI regression asserts that no retry is suggested and nothing is written. Measured on the built CLI: '--message --foo-bar' stores the message '--foo-bar', while '--message --pm-path X' and '--message --output-limit 2' are refused as an argument missing before any read-output refusal.

value.text: CodeRabbit review of PR 1688, two findings declined with reasons. (1) The direct SDK runComments write with outputInclude in its global options: direct SDK primitives never apply universal output controls. A direct runComments read with outputLimit 1 still returns three rows. Shaping is a delivery-layer contract of the CLI and runAction, and runAction (the SDK and MCP transport) refuses the combination with read_output_mutation_conflict. Refusing direct writes would make writes stricter than reads at the same layer. (2) 'pm files discover <id> --apply --output-limit 3' gets the typed refusal but no suggested retry, because no contract source declares --apply: pm contracts --command 'files discover' is unknown_command. Withholding is the designed safe outcome. The contract gap is filed as pm-9ke7h9. A third finding, projection-retry arity for the search-advanced package's --for, concerns the pre-existing projection retry; this PR only moved that scanner, and an ambiguous argv already withholds the retry there.

value.text: CodeRabbit re-review of PR 1688 (Major), fixed. The retry is rebuilt from argv, but an embedded CLI run (PmClient-style, in-process) can execute inside an enclosing SDK withExpectedItemRevisions scope whose guards never reached argv. Run on its own, the retry would write unguarded. src/sdk/lifecycle/item-revision.ts gains isTrackerRevisionGuarded(pmRoot), true when activeItemRevisionExpectations reports guards or unreplayable nested ones. main.ts passes it lazily to repairReadOutputMutationRecovery, so it is evaluated only for this refusal code, and an active guard withholds the retry. Carrying the guards as --expect-hash tokens was not chosen: package-catalog mutations do not accept --expect-hash, and withholding is the safe outcome the refusal already explains. The control-token scan moved into controlTokenIndexes to keep complexity within the cap. docs/READ_OUTPUT_CONTRACTS.md now lists every case in which suggested_retry_args is withheld. Specs: the in-process CLI inside a real revision scope gets no retry, the same argv outside one does, and isTrackerRevisionGuarded covers outer and conflicting nested scopes. The per-surface examples are asserted exactly.

value.text: CodeRabbit round 4 on PR 1688. Fixed (Major): an argv carrying URL userinfo, such as a credentialed package source passed to 'package --catalog --install', now gets no executable retry, so the recovery never repeats the secret in another field. The pre-existing verbatim echo in attempted_command and normalized_args, which every refusal shares, is filed as pm-nhauur. Also fixed: the shared catalog recovery line now reads 'Inspect the structured error guidance, then retry the suggested command when one is present', since a withheld retry has no suggested command. The specs cover the credentialed and plain package sources and check the explicit tracker byte for byte in the two-tracker regression.

value.text: Codex review round 4 on PR 1688 (P2), fixed. The literal '//userinfo@' pattern missed spellings the URL parser normalizes. 'package --catalog --install npm:https:\user:secret@example.invalid/pkg.tgz --output-limit 2' still produced an executable retry containing the credential, although new URL() reads a username and a password from that source. carriesUrlCredentials now parses every URL-scheme suffix of each token, which looks through wrappers such as npm: and git+, and withholds the retry when any candidate has a username or password. The literal pattern stays as a first check. Specs cover the backslash spelling, a wrapped source, a token-only userinfo (git+https://token@host) and the built-CLI repro. They also check that a scoped npm name (npm:@scope/pkg) and the unparseable text 'see http:' still get a retry.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: CodeQL js/polynomial-redos (alert 57) and Codex round 5 on PR 1688 (two P2s), fixed. The unanchored scheme regex /[a-z][a-z\d+.-]*:/g backtracked quadratically on long colon-free text: Codex measured about 15 s for an 80 KB comment. Its matchAll also consumed 'git+https:' as one scheme, so 'npm:git+https:\user:secret@host/repo.git' kept its credential in the retry. carriesUrlCredentials now returns early for a token without '@' (userinfo always ends at one) and otherwise walks at most four candidates: the token itself and each suffix after a ':' or '+' separator, with one URL.canParse each. A token with more nested separators that contains '@' counts as credentialed. Measured on the built CLI: the 80 KB comment is refused in 404 ms, and the npm:git+https: source gets no retry. Specs cover both Codex repros through the built CLI, a 200,000-character token in linear time, the git+https backslash spelling and the deeper-than-the-walk fallback.

value.text: Codex round 6 and Greptile (P2) plus CodeRabbit round 6 on PR 1688. Fixed: an inline option value such as '--add=https:user:secret@host' bypassed credential detection, because the suffix walk advanced past 'https:' before parsing it. urlCandidateStarts now enumerates candidates in one linear pass. For every ':' it takes the run of scheme characters before it, and each letter in that run that starts the run or follows '+', '.' or '-', so inline values and git+ wrappers both yield the inner scheme. It stops at eight candidates, after which a token with '@' counts as credentialed. Also fixed: in '--limit --output-session {} 5 --output-limit 2' the scanner took --output-session as --limit's value, so the retry kept a control and reproduced the conflict. Any control spelling left over now withholds the retry. Declined with reasons: (1) a flat top-level output_include beside nested note-edit options is dropped by runAction before validation, which is the declared-flat-parameter class owned by pm-yjjo4l (scope note there); (2) 'files discover <id> --note ... --output-limit 5' is refused because HYBRID_READ_MUTATION_KEYS has counted note as a files mutation since before this PR, and this PR only typed the refusal (scope note on pm-9ke7h9); (3) an output_format override that moves comment rows to items owns its rendering; (4) a packaged-link checker against the packed inventory is a broader docs tool than this PR.
